caption:
His free video-call training model raised one state's hepatitis-C diagnosis 100x. By training village doctors, not flying in specialists.

Dr. Sanjeev Arora, born in Punjab, founded Project ECHO in 2003 in New Mexico after seeing rural hepatitis-C patients wait 8 months to see one of the state's few specialists - using videoconferencing to let specialists mentor local doctors instead. The model returned to his home country as ECHO India in 2008. In Punjab, a partnership with PGIMER Chandigarh raised hepatitis-C diagnosis from roughly 1,500 to 150,000 patients. The entire model is free and open-source, and has since expanded into tuberculosis treatment and mental-health training in underserved districts.

He didn't send more specialists to rural India. He taught rural India's own doctors to be the specialists it needed.

Sources: ECHO India, Project ECHO (2003-2026)
